name: GPU Direct Volume Rendering with Anisotropic Shading
definition: A ray-casting DVR algorithm on GPU that uses precomputed normals and covariance matrices to perform anisotropic shading using Ward or Lafortune BRDFs.
summary: GPU Direct Volume Rendering with Anisotropic Shading is a GPU-based ray casting algorithm that enhances visual quality by applying anisotropic shading models to volumetric data, distinguishing itself from standard isotropic shading by precomputing and storing covariance matrices alongside gradients.
